rationale: Adopt axios 1.21.0 as the HTTP client. The earlier hold was based on an unverified tree and publish pipeline; both are now verified: axios publishes from GitHub Actions with OIDC trusted publishing and SLSA provenance, the runtime tree is 27 MIT packages with no install scripts, OSV is clean, and a local ESM/CJS interceptor and mock-adapter probe passed. follow-redirects 1.16.2 is adopted only as the required Node transport beneath axios; pin it exactly and record the no-provenance gap. The other five are held for this requirement because none provides the HTTP client, interceptor, global-config or mocking role: undici is a Node-only client already embedded in modern Node, fast-uri is a URI utility, js-cookie and cookie are cookie helpers, and protobufjs is a protobuf codec. The Firebase 13.2.0 tree is context only: it resolves protobufjs 7.6.6, not the reviewed 8.8.1, and does not contain the other four. The board does not need the consuming application's lockfile to make this HTTP client decision.
decided_by: dbs-amoswong; revised by opencode-review (delegated by dbs-amoswong)
scope: HTTP client and required Node transport selection. Application lockfile, bundle measurement and interceptor/mocking regression are consumer obligations.
criteria: Actively maintained and responsive to security reports
No unfixed high or critical advisories
Works in both browser and Node environments
Compatible with the existing axios interceptors, global config and mocking approach
Permissive license across the full dependency tree
No install scripts in the dependency tree
Avoid duplicate or unnecessary direct dependencies
If npm provenance is unavailable, pin exact versions and record the gap

alternatives_considered.name: axios 1.21.0
alternatives_considered.reason: Existing interceptor/global-config/mock client; dual browser/Node; OIDC publish workflow and SLSA provenance verified; 27-package MIT tree with no install scripts; clean advisories; local compatibility probe passed.

alternatives_considered.name: follow-redirects 1.16.2
alternatives_considered.reason: The only verified axios edge; small, zero-dependency MIT Node transport. No npm provenance, so pin exactly and record the gap.

alternatives_considered.name: undici 8.12.3
alternatives_considered.reason: Healthy Node HTTP client, but Node-only, CJS-only and duplicative of the client embedded in modern Node. No verified parent edge in the current tree.

alternatives_considered.name: fast-uri 4.2.3
alternatives_considered.reason: URI utility, not an HTTP client. No verified parent edge in the current tree.

alternatives_considered.name: js-cookie 3.0.8
alternatives_considered.reason: Browser cookie helper; no verified parent edge, no types and no Node evidence.

alternatives_considered.name: cookie 2.0.1
alternatives_considered.reason: Cookie header parser/serialiser, not an HTTP client; ESM-only, Node >=22 and no types. No verified parent edge.

alternatives_considered.name: protobufjs 8.8.1
alternatives_considered.reason: Protobuf codec, not an HTTP client. Firebase 13.2.0 resolves 7.6.6 through @grpc/proto-loader, not the reviewed 8.8.1; re-review the version actually used if it is needed.

alternatives_considered.name: Native fetch
alternatives_considered.reason: The requirement explicitly keeps replacing axios with native fetch out of scope.

conditions: Pin axios 1.21.0 and follow-redirects 1.16.2 exactly, and commit the lockfile.
Record follow-redirects' missing npm provenance in the consuming project.
Keep using axios interceptors, global config and the existing mocking approach; the local probe covered the interceptor and adapter path.

Do not adopt undici, fast-uri, js-cookie, cookie or protobufjs as HTTP clients for this requirement. If a consuming application needs one for a different role, review it against a separate requirement.
Consuming applications that include Firebase should record that it resolves protobufjs 7.6.6, not 8.8.1, and review that version separately if protobuf handling becomes in scope.
Consuming applications own their lockfile, browser bundle measurement and interceptor/mocking regression; this board does not have access to those applications.
Re-check advisories and the axios publish workflow every 90 days.
unknowns: The consuming application's parent chains are outside this board's access; they are context for monitoring, not a condition for this HTTP client decision.
Firebase 13.2.0 pulls protobufjs 7.6.6, not the reviewed 8.8.1.
The browser bundle size and the full application interceptor/mocking suite were not measured; the probe covered the API path.
axios has a single npm maintainer and 110 open issues.
reversal_cost: Low for axios: it is already the client the requirement is built around. Replacing it with native fetch or another client is a separate requirement.
review_triggers: A new high or critical advisory affects axios or follow-redirects.
The axios OIDC publish workflow or provenance attestation changes.
Firebase or another parent starts pulling a different undici, fast-uri, js-cookie, cookie or protobufjs version.
A separate requirement needs a cookie or URI utility.
axios changes maintainership, drops dual browser/Node support or removes the interceptor API.
